story_description: Enable users to create hooks once and migrate them between different agentic CLI providers (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI) with automatic event and tool name translation
task_description: Implement the HookMigrator struct that translates hook definitions between providers by mapping event names, tool names, and configuration formats while preserving hook semantics
atom_description: Build the HookMigrator struct with three core methods: migrateHook() for full hook translation, mapEventName() for event lifecycle mapping between providers, and mapToolName() for provider-specific tool name resolution
problem_statement: Users who configure hooks for one agentic CLI (e.g., Claude Code) cannot reuse those configurations with other CLIs (e.g., Gemini CLI, Codex CLI) because each provider uses different event names, tool names, and configuration formats. This forces users to manually recreate their hook setups for each provider, leading to duplication, inconsistency, and wasted effort.

Implement mapEventName(from:to:event:) method for provider event name translation
Implement mapToolName(from:to:tool:) method for provider tool name translation
Support bidirectional mapping between Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and Codex CLI providers
Define comprehensive event mapping tables for all three providers
Define comprehensive tool mapping tables for all three providers

Emit telemetry events for successful migrations and mapping failures

assumptions: HookNode struct already exists and represents a provider-agnostic hook definition
HookProvider enum exists with cases for claudeCode, geminiCli, and codexCli
Event mapping is deterministic and one-to-one for supported events
Tool names have equivalent semantics across providers even with different naming
Some events and tools may not have equivalents in all providers (partial mapping acceptable)
Blaze logging and telemetry infrastructure is available for integration
constraints: Must use pure Swift with no external dependencies
Must be thread-safe for use from multiple queues
Must not mutate input HookNode - return new instance
Translation must be reversible (migrate A to B, then B to A yields semantically equivalent hook)
Must handle all current hook event types from Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and Codex CLI documentation
Performance: single hook migration must complete in under 1ms
functional_requirements: FR-001: migrateHook(from:to:hook:) shall accept source provider, target provider, and source HookNode and return translated HookNode or nil
FR-002: migrateHook shall translate the hook event name using mapEventName
FR-003: migrateHook shall translate all tool matchers in the hook using mapToolName
FR-004: migrateHook shall preserve hook metadata (name, description, enabled state) unchanged
FR-005: migrateHook shall preserve hook action commands unchanged (shell commands are provider-agnostic)
FR-006: mapEventName(from:to:event:) shall return the equivalent event name in target provider or nil if no mapping exists
FR-007: mapToolName(from:to:tool:) shall return the equivalent tool name in target provider or nil if no mapping exists
FR-008: All three methods shall be static or instance methods on HookMigrator struct
FR-009: Migration shall emit hook.migration.completed telemetry event on success
FR-010: Migration shall emit hook.migration.failed telemetry event with reason on failure
FR-011: Partial migrations (some tools unmappable) shall succeed with warnings logged
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR-001: Thread-safety - HookMigrator must be safe to call from any thread without locks
NFR-002: Performance - single migration under 1ms on M1 Mac
NFR-003: Memory - no allocations beyond the output HookNode
NFR-004: Testability - all mapping tables must be exposed for unit testing
NFR-005: Extensibility - adding new providers must only require extending mapping tables
NFR-006: Error messages must include source event/tool name and both provider names for debugging
implementation_steps: Step 1: Create HookMigrator.swift file in Blaze/Sources/Core/Hooks/ directory
Step 2: Define static mapping dictionaries for Claude-to-Gemini event names
Step 3: Define static mapping dictionaries for Gemini-to-Claude event names
Step 4: Define static mapping dictionaries for Claude-to-Codex event names
Step 5: Define static mapping dictionaries for Codex-to-Claude event names
Step 6: Define static mapping dictionaries for Gemini-to-Codex event names
Step 7: Define static mapping dictionaries for Codex-to-Gemini event names
Step 8: Define static mapping dictionaries for tool names across all three providers
Step 9: Implement mapEventName(from:to:event:) using dictionary lookup with O(1) access
Step 10: Implement mapToolName(from:to:tool:) using dictionary lookup with fallback to identity for universal tools
Step 11: Implement migrateHook(from:to:hook:) composing mapEventName and mapToolName
Step 12: Add telemetry event emission for hook.migration.completed and hook.migration.failed
Step 13: Add structured logging for unmappable events and tools with full context
Step 14: Write unit tests for all event mappings in both directions
Step 15: Write unit tests for all tool mappings in both directions
Step 16: Write integration test for full hook migration round-trip
Step 17: Add documentation comments with examples for all public methods
data_model_changes: No schema changes - HookMigrator operates on existing HookNode and HookProvider types
Add optional migrationSource: HookProvider? field to HookNode for tracking original provider
Add optional originalEventName: String? field to HookNode for debugging round-trip issues
api_contracts: struct HookMigrator with migrateHook(from: HookProvider, to: HookProvider, hook: HookNode) -> HookNode? method
struct HookMigrator with mapEventName(from: HookProvider, to: HookProvider, event: String) -> String? method
struct HookMigrator with mapToolName(from: HookProvider, to: HookProvider, tool: String) -> String? method
All methods are deterministic pure functions with no side effects except telemetry
event_contracts: hook.migration.completed: Emitted when migrateHook succeeds, payload includes sourceProvider, targetProvider, hookId, mappedEventName
hook.migration.failed: Emitted when migrateHook fails, payload includes sourceProvider, targetProvider, hookId, failureReason
hook.mapping.unmappable_event: Emitted when mapEventName returns nil, payload includes event name and both providers
hook.mapping.unmappable_tool: Emitted when mapToolName returns nil, payload includes tool name and both providers
ui_states: Backend-only component with no UI states - HookMigrator is called programmatically from UI code
ui_interactions: Backend-only component with no user interactions - called via HookStore.migrate() from settings UI
ui_copy: Backend-only component with no user-facing text - error messages are for logs and developer debugging only
edge_cases: Same source and target provider (no-op migration should return copy of input)
Hook with event that has no equivalent in target provider (return nil with logged warning)
Hook with multiple tool matchers where some map and some do not (partial migration with warnings)
Empty tool matchers array (should preserve empty array in output)
Hook with wildcard tool matcher '*' (should preserve wildcard unchanged)
Provider enum case not handled in mapping tables (defensive nil return with error log)
Nil or empty event name in input hook (return nil immediately with validation error)
Unicode or special characters in event/tool names (pass through unchanged)
Very long tool matcher lists exceeding 100 items (process all without truncation)
failure_modes: Input hook has nil or empty event name - return nil, log validation error, emit hook.migration.failed
Event name not in mapping table - return nil, log unmappable event, emit hook.mapping.unmappable_event
Internal mapping table inconsistency (missing reverse mapping) - return nil, log internal error
Memory pressure during HookNode allocation - Swift handles via standard error propagation
Thread contention on shared mapping tables - mitigated by using let constants (no locks needed)
rollback_plan: HookMigrator is a pure utility struct with no persistent state. Rollback consists of reverting the HookMigrator.swift file and removing HookMigratorTests.swift. No database migrations or configuration changes to undo. Feature flag hook_migration_enabled can disable UI access to migration without removing code.

risks: Incomplete event mapping tables may cause unexpected nil returns for valid hooks
Tool naming inconsistencies across providers may lead to incorrect mappings
Future provider updates may add new events not in mapping tables
Thread-safety assumptions may be violated if mapping tables are mutated
mitigations: Exhaustively document all known events from each provider's official documentation
Add fallback to identity mapping for tools with identical names across providers
Design mapping tables as extensible dictionaries with clear extension points
Use let constants for all mapping tables to guarantee immutability and thread-safety
risk_register.blast_radius: Low - HookMigrator is a pure utility with no persistent state. Failures result in nil returns, not crashes or data corruption. Worst case is user cannot migrate a specific hook and must recreate manually.
risk_register.fallback_plan: If HookMigrator has critical bugs, feature flag hook_migration_enabled can disable migration UI while keeping manual hook creation functional. Code can be hotfixed independently without affecting other hook functionality.

apis: HookMigrator.migrateHook(from: HookProvider, to: HookProvider, hook: HookNode) -> HookNode? - Returns translated hook or nil if event unmappable
HookMigrator.mapEventName(from: HookProvider, to: HookProvider, event: String) -> String? - Returns mapped event name or nil
HookMigrator.mapToolName(from: HookProvider, to: HookProvider, tool: String) -> String? - Returns mapped tool name or nil, identity for universal tools
state: HookMigrator is stateless - all mapping tables are static let constants
No instance variables, no mutable state, no caching
persistence: No persistence - HookMigrator is a pure transformation utility
Migrated hooks are persisted by caller (HookStore) not by HookMigrator
No database access, no file I/O, no UserDefaults
